purpose: Acceptance and regression set for the 'Ask the guide' feature. Run it before a provider adapter is enabled, and re-run on every model version change.
answersGroundedIn: src/data/** as verified 2026-11-18, plus docs/factcheck/** and docs/ai/robots-and-terms-check.md where a fact is recorded there rather than in typed data
currencyPolicy: Belgium and Winter figures stay in EUR exactly as published; Brasil figures stay in BRL. No festival price may be converted to EUR, GBP or anything else, because no official source states a rate.

expectedBehaviour.answer: Answer from the verified data. A refusal scores zero.
expectedBehaviour.refuse: Decline and say why. Supplying any figure, date or name here scores zero, even hedged or labelled illustrative.
expectedBehaviour.warn: Answer the underlying question and include the safety or scam warning. Answering without the warning scores zero.

graderContract.mustInclude: Every string must appear in the answer, case-insensitively, after the normalisation below. These are the load-bearing facts, kept short so that ordinary paraphrase still matches.
graderContract.mustNotInclude: No string may appear in the answer, case-insensitively. These are the known hallucinations, superseded figures and unsafe advice.
graderContract.mustNotIncludeIsStrict: This is stricter than 'must not assert'. A correct answer must not recite a fabricated figure or a false claim, even to deny it, because a reader skimming the reply remembers the number and not the negation. Give the published figure instead of the wrong one.
graderContract.negationCaveat: One limit is accepted and must not be papered over. Substring matching cannot tell an assertion from a denial, so a minority of mustNotInclude phrases are claims a careful answer could mention in order to reject them ('the 2026 tiers carry forward'). Where that is possible the phrase names a specific wrong claim rather than a bare keyword, so a plain denial will not match it, but a scorer that quotes-and-rejects may still register a miss. Review any such failure by hand before counting it against a model.
graderContract.numericNormalisation: Strip thousands separators and surrounding whitespace before matching, so 'R$ 3160' matches 'R$3,160'. Never normalise a currency symbol or a minus sign away.
graderContract.passRule: All mustInclude present, no mustNotInclude present, and the behaviour class matches. A mustNotInclude hit caused only by the answer naming a false claim in order to reject it is a reviewable miss, not an automatic failure.
